questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Types of Economic Systems' refers to.
questions.a: An economic framework determining how a society answers the central questions of production, method, and distribution, broadly categorized into capitalist, socialist, and mixed economies.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Types of Economic Systems'.
questions.a: Societies allocate resources through market forces, central government planning, or a combination of both.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Types of Economic Systems' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2.1 (source: keec102.txt lines 30-85)

concepts.title: Five Year Plans and Perspective Planning

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Five Year Plans and Perspective Planning' refers to.
questions.a: A structured national policy framework defining resource allocation and development targets over a five-year period, guided by a long-term vision spanning twenty years.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Five Year Plans and Perspective Planning'.
questions.a: Five-year plans operationalize immediate goals while serving the broader objectives of long-term perspective plans.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Five Year Plans and Perspective Planning' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2.1 (source: keec102.txt lines 86-120)

concepts.title: Gross Domestic Product and Economic Growth

questions.q: Calculate gross domestic product from sectoral contributions. Use the method 'Gross Domestic Product and Economic Growth'. Work with: agri_output = 8, ind_output = 400, service_output = 400. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 808 rupees

questions.q: Find total GDP given output of agriculture, industry, and services. Use the method 'Gross Domestic Product and Economic Growth'. Work with: agri_output = 18, ind_output = 120, service_output = 75. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 213 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Gross Domestic Product and Economic Growth' refers to.
questions.a: Economic growth represents the continuous expansion of a country's total output of goods and services, quantified by the aggregate value produced across all sectors.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Gross Domestic Product and Economic Growth'.
questions.a: GDP expansion reflects an increase in national productive capacity and overall economic activity.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Gross Domestic Product and Economic Growth', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: gdp = agri_output + ind_output + service_output

questions.q: Calculate the percentage contribution of a sector to GDP. Use the method 'Structural Composition of GDP'. Work with: gdp = 1200, sector_output = 5. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 0.4167 per cent

questions.q: Find the sectoral share of agriculture or industry in total output. Use the method 'Structural Composition of GDP'. Work with: gdp = 20000, sector_output = 15. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 0.075 per cent

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Structural Composition of GDP' refers to.
questions.a: The relative proportion or percentage share that agriculture, industry, and service sectors contribute to the overall Gross Domestic Product.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Structural Composition of GDP'.
questions.a: Economic development typically involves a shift in GDP share from primary agriculture toward industry and services.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Structural Composition of GDP', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: sector_share = (sector_output / gdp) * 100

concepts.title: Planning Goals: Modernisation, Self-Reliance, and Equity

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Planning Goals: Modernisation, Self-Reliance, and Equity' refers to.
questions.a: The core socioeconomic pillars of planning designed to adopt modern techniques and progressive social mindsets, minimize foreign dependency, and ensure fair distribution of wealth.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Planning Goals: Modernisation, Self-Reliance, and Equity'.
questions.a: Balancing technological advancement and self-sufficiency with social justice ensures economic benefits reach all strata.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Planning Goals: Modernisation, Self-Reliance, and Equity' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2.2 (source: keec102.txt lines 191-240)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Land Reforms and Land Ceiling' refers to.
questions.a: Institutional restructuring of agrarian ownership involving the elimination of intermediaries to transfer land to actual tillers, paired with legal limits on maximum land ownership per individual.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Land Reforms and Land Ceiling'.
questions.a: Granting land ownership to cultivators enhances productivity incentives while ceilings curb land concentration.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Land Reforms and Land Ceiling' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2.3 (source: keec102.txt lines 241-310)

questions.q: Calculate the marketed surplus of food grains. Use the method 'Green Revolution and Marketed Surplus'. Work with: farm_consumption = 15, total_production = 75. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 60 rupees

questions.q: Find the quantity of agricultural produce available for market sale. Use the method 'Green Revolution and Marketed Surplus'. Work with: farm_consumption = 30, total_production = 75. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 45 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Green Revolution and Marketed Surplus' refers to.
questions.a: The dramatic increase in food grain production resulting from High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, chemical inputs, and controlled irrigation, enabling farmers to sell surplus grain in open markets.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Green Revolution and Marketed Surplus'.
questions.a: The excess of crop yield over personal consumption generates marketed surplus, lowering market food prices and building national reserves.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Green Revolution and Marketed Surplus', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: marketed_surplus = total_production - farm_consumption

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Debate Over Agricultural Subsidies' refers to.
questions.a: The policy disagreement regarding whether government financial assistance on farm inputs should be continued to protect vulnerable farmers or eliminated to prevent fiscal drain and resource waste.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Debate Over Agricultural Subsidies'.
questions.a: Subsidies lower adoption risks for small farmers but can cause environmental harm and financial strain if misallocated.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Debate Over Agricultural Subsidies' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2.3 (source: keec102.txt lines 371-430)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 (IPR 1956)' refers to.
questions.a: A foundational policy document that classified industries into state-monopolized, state-led mixed, and private categories, controlling private activity through mandatory government licensing.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 (IPR 1956)'.
questions.a: IPR 1956 prioritized public sector command of core industries while using industrial licensing to promote balanced regional growth.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 (IPR 1956)' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2.4 (source: keec102.txt lines 431-510)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Small-Scale Industry (SSI) and Development' refers to.
questions.a: Industrial units defined by capital investment limits on fixed assets, prioritized for their high capacity to generate employment using labor-intensive methods.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Small-Scale Industry (SSI) and Development'.
questions.a: Small-scale enterprises drive rural employment and distribution of income, requiring state protection from large-scale competitors.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Small-Scale Industry (SSI) and Development' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2.4 (source: keec102.txt lines 511-545)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Import Substitution and Trade Protection' refers to.
questions.a: An inward-focused trade policy designed to substitute foreign imports with domestic production using protective tariffs and quantitative import quotas.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Import Substitution and Trade Protection'.
questions.a: Protecting young domestic industries from foreign competition conserves foreign exchange and promotes domestic self-reliance.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Import Substitution and Trade Protection' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2.5 (source: keec102.txt lines 546-600)
